notes:
Lead origin: inbound from Zapier marketplace listing + blog post on ticket summarization. Customer profile: small SaaS that sells a no-code chat widget for SMBs; currently integrates with Zendesk and uses webhook-based automations. They want an easy hosted API to power: 1) automatic ticket summarization (2–3 sentences) stored in 'agent_summary' field, 2) structured extraction of ticket metadata (priority, topic tags, customer sentiment) as JSON, 3) tool-calling to create/update tickets and add internal notes.

Trial activity: signed up self-serve on 2026-03-05, used free credits to run ~1.2M tokens across test batch (50–100 tickets) in sandbox. Ran with third-party API previously (higher cost); primary driver to evaluate Redwood is lower per-token cost and enforced structured output + tool-calling reliability.

Technical requirements / P0s:
- Structured JSON output enforced by schema; must fail-safe to human-readable fallback when validation fails.
- Tool-calling hooks for Zendesk: create_ticket, add_internal_note, escalate_to_agent. Need examples and SDK snippets.
- Latency: acceptable median response time ~200–500ms for single-turn summarization; burst capacity for peak support hours (~50 req/s).
- Cost: target cost-per-ticket (gen+embedding) < $0.02 to keep margins for SMB customers — CTO quote: "If cost is above that we reprice our product".
- Security: SOC2 is required within 6–9 months; SSO optional for now. Audit logs and ability to purge PII on request are must-haves.

POC notes:
- POC scope: 1) Summarization pipeline using hosted_api + embeddings for triage, 2) Tool-calling demo to update Zendesk ticket fields, 3) Sample structured-output schema with automatic validation.
- POC metrics they will watch: latency p50/p95, tokens per ticket, failed-schema rate, cost per 1k tickets.
